name: 3d-ar-studio-mcp

tools.name: generate_3d_model
tools.description: Turn a text prompt into a textured, downloadable 3D model (GLB). Free and keyless. Describe a SINGLE object, character, or creature: "a brass mid-century desk lamp", not a whole scene. Returns the model URL plus links that open it in the viewer, in the user's room through their phone camera, and in the AR studio. Use kind:"avatar" for a character: it comes back rigged, so it idles and animates instead of standing in a T-pose.

prompt.description: The single object or character to model.

kind.description: model (a prop, default), avatar (a rigged character), or mesh (art-directed, prompt refined first).

tools.name: check_generation
tools.description: Collect a 3D generation that was still rendering when generate_3d_model returned. Pass the job_id from that result. While it is still working you get updated timing; when it is done you get the model.

job_id.description: The job_id from a pending generation.

tools.name: search_models
tools.description: Search the ready-made 3D model catalogue by name, category and tag. The default catalogue is a few hundred public-domain (CC0) props, free to use commercially. Faster and more predictable than generating when a common object will do: search first, generate what you cannot find.

query.description: Words to match against names, categories and tags. Omit to browse.

limit.description: How many results to return. Default 12.

catalogue.description: A different catalogue URL to search instead of the default.

tools.name: compose_ar_scene
tools.description: Arrange several models into a single scene and get one link that reopens it exactly: same models, same positions, rotations and scales. Open that link on a phone and the whole arrangement stands in the real room. Coordinates are metres on the floor: x is right, z is forward with negative values further away, so { x: 0, z: -2 } is two metres in front of the viewer. This is the tool to reach for when someone wants to see more than one thing at once.

x.description: Metres right of the viewer. Default 0.

z.description: Metres in front of the viewer, negative is further away. Default -1.6.

yaw.description: Rotation in radians about the vertical axis.

models.description: The models to arrange, in placement order.

page_url.description: The page hosting the studio. Defaults to the hosted demo.

title.description: A name for the scene, used in the summary.

tools.name: export_ar
tools.description: Turn any public GLB URL into a one-tap "View in your space" experience. The returned link routes itself by device: Apple Quick Look on iPhone and iPad, Google Scene Viewer on Android, an interactive WebGL viewer on desktop. Use it right after generating or finding a model so the person can put it on their actual desk.

glb_url.description: Public https URL of a .glb or .gltf model.

title.description: Name shown in the AR experience.

kind.description: avatar marks a rigged character, which stays animated.

user_agent.description: If you know the viewer's User-Agent, the response names the viewer they will get.

tools.name: create_ar_page
tools.description: Return a complete, self-contained HTML page that embeds the AR studio, configured for the caller's models. Write it to a file, commit it, and it works on GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, or any static host: no build step and no API key. Use it when someone asks to "add AR to my site" rather than just to see a model.

assets.description: Catalogue URL for the model tray. Defaults to the free CC0 library.

x.description: Metres right of the viewer. Default 0.

z.description: Metres in front of the viewer, negative is further away. Default -1.6.

yaw.description: Rotation in radians about the vertical axis.

models.description: Models pre-loaded into the scene on open.

generate.description: Show the text-to-3D prompt box. Default true.

instructions: Put 3D things in a person's real room. Search the ready-made library first (search_models) and generate only what you cannot find (generate_3d_model). For more than one object, arrange them with compose_ar_scene and give the person the single link it returns: that link reopens the whole arrangement in their room. Always hand back a link rather than only a .glb file: a bare model file is not something a person can look at. AR links are meant to be opened on a phone.
